1 Faculty SenateFebruary 1, 2006Faculty Senate Curricular Affairs CommitteeFour Hundred and Thirty-Ninth ReportProposal for the Establishment of the Department of Physical Therapy as aSeparate Academic DepartmentAt its meeting of January 31, 2006, The Curricular Affairs Committeeapproved the following proposal for the establishment of the Department ofPhysical Therapy as a separate academic department and recommendsconfirmation by the Faculty Senate. The proposal is in the format required bythe Board of Governors for Higher Education. A.GENERAL INFORMATION1. Name of institutionUniversity of Rhode Island2. Names of administrative unitsKinesiology DepartmentCollege of Human Science and Services3. Title of proposed organizational unitPhysical Therapy Department4. Intended date of changeUpon Board of Governors approval5. Intended location of organizational unitUniversity of Rhode Island, Kingston Campus

2 6. Institutional review and approval processApproval DatePhysical Therapy Program FacultyMarch 3, 2004Kinesiology DepartmentApril 22, 2004Human Science & ServicesCurriculum CommitteeSept. 14, 2005Human Science & Services College FacultyOct. 19, 2005Faculty Senate Curricular Affairs CommitteeJanuary 31, 2006Faculty SenateFebruary 23, 2006President of the UniversityMarch 1, 20067. Summary description of the proposed organization change.The purpose of this proposal is to change the standing of the PhysicalTherapy Program from a program within the Kinesiology Department toa separate Department within the College of Human Science andServices.8. Signature of the President ______________________________Robert L. Carothers9. ResourcesThe organizational changes proposed herein require no new resources.The Physical Therapy Program has its own director, faculty,secretarial support, facilities, and operating budget.10. Person to be contacted during the reviewDiane HormAssociate DeanCollege of Human Science and Servicesdiane@uri.edu874-2403Beth Marcoux, PT, PhDProgram DirectorPhysical Therapybmarcoux@mail.uri.edu874-562711. Signed agreements for cooperative arrangements.None

3 B.RATIONALEThis organizational change is being proposed because the Physical TherapyProgram can better fulfill its mission to educate competent doctors ofphysical therapy who can provide skilled patient care in a variety ofsettings, conduct clinical research, and provide service to the communityat large if it is an academic department within the College of HumanScience and Services rather than a program within the KinesiologyDepartment.
The mission of the Physical Therapy Program focuses onprofessional, graduate rather than undergraduate education as is the casein the Kinesiology Department.
There are no common students between thetwo units nor does faculty teach across the units.
The reorganization willallow PT faculty to focus their efforts on continued development andadvancement of the program, clinical and basic science research related tothe profession and provision of service to the community and profession.The Physical Therapy Program has functioned autonomously within the(Department of Physical Education now renamed) Kinesiology Departmentsince its inception in 1991.

It has had its own faculty, support staff,facilities, and budget from the very beginning as a requirement ofprofessional accreditation.
Further, due to accreditation requirements,the Program Director has maintained direct communication with the Deanof the College and was a regular participant at College Managementmeetings.
A self-study report for the Commission on Accreditation inPhysical Therapy Education was recently completed in preparation for asite visit that occurred in September 2005.
It was during this self-evaluation that the faculty recognized that the Program was intended tobe a separate entity within the college from its development and thatseparation would allow for better overall functioning of the program.With the recent move from the masters of physical therapy to thedoctor of physical therapy, the program is even more out of place beinglocated within the Kinesiology Department.
Separation will allow bettercollaboration between the Physical Therapy Program and otherdepartments such as Communicative Disorders and Biology.

This re-organization will simplify day-to-day operations and clarify evaluation ofprogram activities because data will no longer be combined with that ofthe Kinesiology department.
Please note that no new resources areneeded to affect this organizational change.C.INSTITUTIONAL ROLEThis organizational change is consistent with the published role and missionof URI.
The Department of Physical Therapy will have all of theresponsibilities of a Department.
In addition, it will provide added value tothe University through its recognition as the only Physical TherapyProgram in the state and via the clinic, which provides physical therapy tocitizens of Rhode Island.

4 D.INTERINSTITUTIONAL CONSIDERATIONSThe projected impact of this organizational change on the other publichigher educational institutions in Rhode Island is nil. Other institutions inRhode Island will not be affected by this change because the PhysicalTherapy Program is not a new program and is not competing with otherprograms in the state for students or resources.There are no cooperative arrangements with other institutions relative tothis organizational change.E.EVALUATIONThe Physical Therapy Program is fully accredited through the Commissionon Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE). Evaluation ofthe program is on going and includes both direct and indirect measures ofclearly defined outcomes. Examples of outcome measures include thepercentage of students who pass the National Physical Therapy LicensureExam, the percentage of students who receive outstanding grades on theclinical performance instrument, a tool that is used nationally to evaluatethe performance of students in the clinical setting, and responses fromemployers gathered both on surveys and in focus groups. Effective thissemester, the PT program will begin using the electronic portfolio systemrecently purchased by URI called “True Outcomes”. Data from theseevaluations will be used to make necessary changes in the doctor ofphysical therapy degree program.

Summary of Proposed Organizational Change The College of Pharmacy presently consists of three Departments: The Department of Applied Pharmaceutical Science (APS); The Department of Biomedical Science (BMS) and the Department of Pharmacy Practice (PHP). The Department of APS consists of two sections, a Pharmaceutics Section and a Pharmacoepidemiology / Pharmaceconomics Section. During the 2002-2003 academic year the Dean of the College established a committee with representation from all three departments. The committee was charged to consider ways of optimizing the administration, research program and teaching activities of the College. After discussions with the Dean of the College, it was recommended that the College be reorganized into two departments. It was proposed that the Pharmaceutics Section of APS and the whole of BMS should be merged to form a new Department of Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Sciences (BPS). It was further proposed that the Pharmacoepidemiology and Pharmacoeconomics section of APS become part of the Department of PHP. 9. RATIONALE The College of Pharmacy presently consists of three Departments: The Department of Applied Pharmaceutical Science (APS); The Department of Biomedical Science (BMS) and the Department of Pharmacy Practice (PHP).
Faculty in PHP are primarily clinicians, who are directly involved in patient care and as a result are primarily based at clinical sites throughout the state.
In contrast, faculty in APS a nd BMS are based at the Kingston campus.
Furthermore, with the exception of the Pharmacoepidemiology and Pharmacoeconomics (PE/PE) Section of APS, the research activities of APS and BMS are primarily laboratory based.
As pharmaceutical science and biomedical science has evolved in the last decade there has been an increasing overlap in the research activities of the two departments.
However, the present departmental structure discourages collaboration and hinders interaction between and among faculty.
